Nxeon is a VPS/game-server hosting platform (Next.js 15 app, Postgres via Prisma). You must do ALL your work inside /opt/nxeon-agent-dm — this is a pre-prepared git worktree on its own branch (agent-admin-dm), completely separate from the main /opt/nxeon working tree which another process is actively using concurrently. Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon itself. cd into /opt/nxeon-agent-dm first and stay there for everything (reads, edits, tsc, tests). node_modules and .env are already symlinked in for you. When done, commit your work there (to the existing agent-admin-dm branch — do NOT create a different branch, do NOT merge to main, do NOT push, do NOT run any deploy script) and report back the summary. IMPORTANT: never run `git add -A` or `git add .` in this worktree — node_modules is a symlink and a broad add can stage it in a way that corrupts the real one elsewhere; always `git add` specific files by name.

**The ask**: staff currently have two ways to reach a customer with a specific message: the support-ticket system (customer-initiated) and live chat (also customer-initiated, see components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx). There's no way for STAFF to proactively send a direct message/ping to one specific customer without either the customer having opened a ticket first, or staff creating a whole new ticket on the customer's behalf (which is heavier-weight and shows up as a formal ticket in their history rather than a quick note). The owner wants an easy way for admin/staff to directly message an individual customer — something lighter-weight than opening a ticket, for things like "hey, noticed X on your server, wanted to give you a heads up" or "following up on Y."

Investigate the existing codebase thoroughly before designing anything:
1. Look at the existing `Notification` model (prisma/schema.prisma) and how in-app notifications currently work (worker code creates them, e.g. `db.notification.create`) — is a notification currently one-directional (system → customer) with no reply capability? Check the customer-facing UI that renders notifications.
2. Look at the existing Ticket/TicketMessage system (lib/actions-support.ts, components/admin/TicketControls.tsx) and the live-chat system (lib/actions-chat.ts, components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx) to understand the two existing patterns for staff-customer communication, their permission model (see lib/staff-grants.ts for the `supportTickets`/`liveChat` area-based access pattern used throughout this codebase), and their UI conventions (message bubbles, read receipts, etc. — components/admin/TicketControls.tsx's ReplyForm and the CannedReplyPicker are relevant recent examples of this UI style).
3. Decide the right shape for a lightweight admin-initiated DM: most likely a new lightweight message thread model (or extending Notification with a reply capability) that's visibly distinct from a formal support ticket in the customer's dashboard, but still lets the customer see and respond to it. Consider reusing as much of the existing Ticket/TicketMessage plumbing and UI components as sensibly possible (read receipts, attachment support, canned-reply picker) rather than building a fully parallel system from scratch — but the KEY functional distinction from a ticket must be preserved: staff can INITIATE this without the customer having done anything first, and it should not clutter the customer's formal "Tickets" list/count the same way (consider whether it should be its own inbox/tab, or a special ticket status/origin flag that changes how it displays — pick a clean, well-reasoned design and explain the tradeoff in your final report).
4. Implement it: the DB model/migration (this project uses `prisma db push`, not migration files — check prisma/schema.prisma's existing conventions), the server actions (following the same requireAnyGrant/staff-grants permission pattern as the rest of admin support code), the admin-side UI (a way to start a new DM to any customer, e.g. from their Customer 360 view or user detail page — check app/admin/users/[id] for a natural place to add a "Message customer" action), and the customer-facing UI to see and reply to it.

Since this project has no migrations folder (schema-push workflow only, confirmed in existing docs/memory), do NOT attempt to run `prisma db push` against a live database from your worktree — that would need a real DATABASE_URL write and could affect the shared database another process is also using concurrently. Just write the correct schema change in prisma/schema.prisma and all the application code; note clearly in your final report that `prisma db push` still needs to be run for real once this is reviewed and merged.

Before finishing: run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (schema-dependent type errors from the un-pushed model are expected and fine to note, but everything else should be clean) and `npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts`, comparing against the pre-existing baseline failure count (git stash comparison) to confirm you haven't introduced unrelated regressions. Note: a pre-existing baseline of ~35 unrelated failures (billing/pricing/auth tests) is already known and expected.

Report back with: the design decision you made (data model shape, how it's visually/functionally distinguished from a ticket) and why, which files changed, and the typecheck/test status.

content.thinking:
The Support page combines Tickets, Live Chat, Help, and Status as tabs in one SupportView component, so a natural spot to add "Messages from Nxeon staff" would be a new tab or folded into Tickets. Given the scope—a full new UI screen on both admin and customer sides plus reusing components—this is substantial, so I need to nail down design decisions quickly before implementing.

I'm deciding to add a lightweight new model for staff-initiated direct message threads, separate from Ticket but following a similar pattern: a thread record tied to the customer and the staff member who started it, with a subject, open/closed status, and a related messages table for the individual message bodies.

The key point is that these DMs shouldn't affect the Tickets list or count, since staff can start them without customer action. I'm giving them their own tab—something like "Messages"—alongside Tickets, Live Chat, Help Center, and Status on the customer's Support page, plus a matching section on the admin's user detail page.

A separate model keeps the Ticket model's semantics clean (priority, SLA reporting, Discord bridge mirroring) rather than scattering a nullable origin flag through every ticket query. Reusing TicketMessage with a nullable polymorphic ticketId would be messier, so a distinct StaffDm/StaffDmMessage model is cleaner, while I can still reuse UI components like ReplyComposer, CannedReplyPicker, and the message bubble structure. Now I'm sketching the Prisma schema for these new models, adding relations on User, and figuring out unread tracking for badge counts on both customer and staff sides.

For the admin experience, I want to check ChatInbox.tsx and actions-chat.ts to see how the existing "inbox across customers" pattern works for live chat, since admins will likely want a top-level DM inbox listing all threads rather than just a per-customer view embedded in Customer 360 -- though the ask specifically mentions starting a DM from the Customer 360 view too.

Given effort constraints, I'll scope this down to: schema models for the DM feature, plus a lib/actions-staff-dm.ts file containing server actions for starting a DM thread with first message (gated by requireAnyGrant), staff replies, customer replies, listing DMs for a user (for the Customer 360 embed), and fetching a single DM thread.

For permissions, I'll reuse the existing "supportTickets" grant area rather than introducing a new one, since it's the same staff handling both tickets and DMs -- keeps things consistent and simpler.

For the admin UI, I'm planning a "Message customer" button on the Customer 360 page that opens a compose form calling startStaffDm, plus a section listing existing DM threads for that user.

I also want a dedicated thread view page mirroring the support ticket thread view, reusing the reply composer and canned reply picker components, and I'm leaning toward adding a lightweight admin inbox page listing all DM threads so staff can find and respond to conversations beyond just the ones started from a specific customer's page.

I should briefly check the chat actions file and existing chat/support view components to borrow their patterns, especially for rendering message bubbles, so the new DM views stay consistent with the rest of the admin UI.

## Summary

**Design decision.** Added `StaffDm`/`StaffDmMessage` as new Prisma models, deliberately separate from `Ticket`/`TicketMessage` rather than a "staff-initiated" flag on Ticket. A Ticket's whole shape assumes the customer opened it (`createTicketCore` always attributes the opening message to the ticket's own `userId`; `priority`/status model an SLA queue; the Discord bridge mirrors every ticket) — retrofitting a flag would leave every one of those consumers silently wrong unless they remembered to check it. The new model reuses `TicketMessage`'s proven shape (read receipt, one attachment) and as much UI/action plumbing as sensibly possible (`ReplyComposer`, `CannedReplyPicker`, `TicketBody`, `ReadReceipt`, the same `requireAnyGrant(["supportTickets"])` permission gate), but is never counted in or listed alongside a customer's formal tickets — it gets its own "Messages" tab on the customer Support page and its own "Direct messages" section/inbox on the admin side, so a quick heads-up never inflates ticket history/counts or trips ticket-only automation.

**Key files:**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — new `StaffDm`/`StaffDmMessage` models + `User` relations (heavily commented, marked NOT YET PUSHED).
- `lib/actions-staff-dm.ts` — `startStaffDm`, `replyStaffDm`, `setStaffDmStatus`, `markStaffDmReadForStaff`, `getStaffDmThread`, each self-guarded per this codebase's `test/auth-lockouts.test.ts` convention.
- `lib/staff-dm-db.ts` — a single `dmDb` unchecked-cast helper (mirrors the existing `lib/discord-bridge.ts` pattern for not-yet-pushed schema) so every call site isn't littered with `as any`.
- Admin: `components/admin/MessageCustomerButton.tsx` (new control on `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`, plus a "Direct messages" table there), `components/admin/StaffDmThreadView.tsx` + `StaffDmControls.tsx`, `app/admin/dms/page.tsx` + `[id]/page.tsx` (inbox + thread), a sidebar tab/badge in `lib/admin-groups.ts`/`app/admin/layout.tsx`.
- Customer: `components/nx/DmMessagesPanel.tsx` (new "Messages" tab in `components/nx/SupportView.tsx`), `components/customer/DmReplyForm.tsx`, wired up in `app/dashboard/support/page.tsx`.
- Attachments: `app/api/dms/attachment/[id]/route.ts` + `components/support/DmMessageAttachment.tsx`, reusing the existing `lib/ticket-attachment.ts` validator.
